key_insight: Normalizing each velocity defect and Reynolds-stress component by its own value at a shared outer-layer location reveals component-wise outer similarity across strong adverse-pressure gradients.
engineering_relevance: Explicit normalized outer profiles offer compact references for assessing APG turbulence models and conditionally reconstructing boundary-layer profiles.
method: Combine a new separation-bubble DNS with published turbulent boundary-layer profiles.
Normalize two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components at y_s = 0.5δ.
Evaluate profile collapse and its sensitivity to the outer-layer reference location.
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans β_e = 0.04–180 and Re_θ = 530–19,000, with collapse emerging at y/δ ≳ 0.2 for velocity defects and ≳ 0.4 for Reynolds stresses.
watch_item: The demonstrated similarity is component-wise and outer-layer-specific; profile reconstruction still requires each quantity's reference amplitude.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
